name: Teferi's Protection
oracle_text:
Until your next turn, your life total can't change and you gain protection from everything. All permanents you control phase out. (While they're phased out, they're treated as though they don't exist. They phase in before you untap during your untap step.)
Exile Teferi's Protection.
blocked_sentences: Until your next turn, your life total can't change and you gain protection from everything.

needs.what: grant_protection must be able to name a *player* as the recipient (a `player` spec beside `objects`), to grant the quality "everything" rather than only a list of colours/types/subtypes, and to last `until_your_next_turn` instead of only until end of turn -- and every rule that reads protection (targeting, damage, enchanting, blocking) has to consult a player's protection set, not just an object's
needs.why_existing_wont_do: grant_protection resolves its recipients through choose_objects and then skips any oid that is not `on_battlefield`, so a player can never receive it; its qualities are built only from `from_colors` (each entry loader-validated against KNOWN_COLORS), `from_types` and `from_subtypes`, none of which can express "everything"; and it writes an `until_eot` TempEffect that cleanup ends this turn, so the "until your next turn" clock does not exist for it. `characteristics.protection_from(state, oid)` is object-keyed throughout, so there is no player-side reader either. `grant_keyword` is not a substitute: protection is parameterised and a Keyword is a bare string.

needs.what: a player-scoped, duration-bounded (`until_your_next_turn`) replacement that stops *every* change to a life total in both directions -- life gain, life loss, life paid as a cost, and the life-loss half of damage -- so the total is frozen rather than merely shielded
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `replace_life_loss` is the closest thing and falls short three ways: it is a `static_effect`, so only a permanent can carry it and an Instant's `spell_effects` cannot install one; it multiplies the magnitude of a loss (`loss_multiplier`) rather than forbidding the change, and a multiplier of 0 would still be a downward-only rewrite; and it is wired only into `primitives.lose_life` and the loss half of `primitives.damage_player`, so `gain_life` moves the total straight past it. The `prevent_damage` op is player-scoped but stops only damage -- its docstring states the only implemented duration is `this_turn` -- leaving ordinary life loss and all life gain free to move the total.
